title: Failover and Recovery Procedures
description: Implement robust failover and recovery procedures for Redis Cluster and Sentinel deployments.

data.text: Failover is the process of promoting a replica to master when the current master fails. Recovery involves bringing failed nodes back into the cluster and rebalancing data. Both procedures must be well-understood and tested to ensure minimal downtime and data integrity.

In Redis Cluster, the failover process is automatic. When a majority of master nodes cannot reach a given master, it is flagged as failing. The cluster then initiates an election among the failed master's replicas. The replica with the most recent data (least replication offset) typically wins the election and is promoted to master.

data.caption: Automatic failover sequence when a master node fails
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant M as Failed Master
    participant R as Replica
    participant S1 as Sentinel/Majority Masters
    participant C as Clients

    M->>S1: Connection lost
    S1->>S1: Quorum detects failure
    S1->>R: Initiate election
    R->>S1: Request votes
    S1->>R: Vote granted (quorum)
    R->>R: Promote to master
    R->>S1: Announce new master
    S1->>C: Update routing configuration
    C->>R: Redirect writes to new master

data.text: A split-brain occurs when two nodes believe they are the master simultaneously, typically after a network partition heals. Redis prevents this by requiring a majority vote before any promotion. If a network partition isolates a minority of masters, they cannot elect a new master because they lack quorum, and they enter an error state for their owned slots.

data.title: Split-Brain Risk
data.text: Never use odd numbers of master nodes without quorum enforcement. If you have 2 masters and the network splits, both sides can promote a replica independently, causing data divergence.

When automatic mechanisms fail or when recovering a node after extended downtime, manual intervention may be necessary. Common recovery tasks include: forcing a replica to take over as master, reinitializing a failed node, and resharding data after adding a new node.

data.title: Forcing a Failover with Redis CLI (Sentinel)
data.code:
# Connect to any Sentinel instance
redis-cli -p 26379

# Force failover of 'mymaster' (useful for testing or emergencies)
SENTINEL FAILOVER mymaster

# Verify the new master
SENTINEL MASTERS
SENTINEL SLAVES mymaster

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Redis Cluster failover is automatic but requires a quorum of masters
Replicas with the highest replication offset win elections
Split-brain is prevented by requiring majority votes for all promotions
Manual recovery is needed for data loss scenarios or cluster resizing
data.takeaway: Automatic failover handles routine failures, but always have a tested manual recovery runbook for edge cases.
